activePlan.objective: Owner-requested: promote development's outstanding commits to main, then build a permanent, automated release -> main promotion path so this doesn't need manual PR/merge handling every time.
steps: Diagnose why a direct git push of the promotion content to main was rejected: main's ruleset requires the 'block' status check, which can only complete via a pull request or a push to development, never in time for a raw push landing on main.

Discover a second, structural blocker: a normal development -> main pull request for the promotion is impossible because PR #9 (the permanent, never-merge monitoring hook) already occupies the only pull request slot GitHub allows between those two branches.
With the owner's explicit permission, create a new permanent 'release' branch as the promotion gate.

Merge main into development first to align history (main's tip had diverged as its own PR #8 merge commit with no unique content), fast-forward release to development's validated tip, open PR #10 (release -> main), confirm every check green, merge it.

Per the owner's follow-up request, automate the release -> main path: add .github/workflows/promote-release.yml (push:release trigger) that opens or reuses the release -> main pull request, waits for every check, and merges only if they all pass.
Document the release branch, the direct-push-to-main prohibition, and the automation in AGENTS.md's branch policy; add a matching test in test/workflow.test.js.
Run the full local suite plus every fast/offline audit before pushing.

completed: PR #10 (release -> main) merged as 63a42ec: main now carries all of development's previously-outstanding commits.

Added .github/workflows/promote-release.yml: on push to release, opens/reuses a release -> main pull request, waits for every check via `gh pr checks --watch`, then merges via `gh pr merge --merge` only if they all pass. Never pushes to main directly, never bypasses or weakens any required check.

AGENTS.md's branch policy now documents: never push directly to main even with explicit instruction (explains exactly why, referencing the block check + PR #9 slot conflict), the release branch's purpose, and that release is a one-time explicit exception to the no-new-branches rule, not a precedent for creating further branches.
Added a new test/workflow.test.js test asserting promote-release.yml's trigger, permissions, gh pr list/create/checks/merge invocations, and the corresponding AGENTS.md documentation.
verification: Full local suite passes 204/204 + 1 new test (205 total).
lint:workflows, docs:check, validate, audit:clutter, audit:privacy, and audit:security all pass.
remaining: Push this commit to development, confirm Self-Test/CodeQL/AI handoff policy green, then fast-forward release to it - this promotes promote-release.yml itself through its own new automated path for the first time. Confirm that first automated run actually opens and merges the pull request correctly.
The owner should confirm 'block' is added as a required status check on main (Settings -> Branches -> Branch protection rules) if not already done - no tool available here can do that remotely.

Still blocked on owner-supplied resources, not a code gap: the hosted multi-repository integration workflow and connect-workflow.yml's activate phase both need a real target repository/token to actually be exercised.
Codex's own remaining items still stand: no promotion or branch-protection change is authorized without the owner's explicit instruction beyond what's already been done.
